title: Human Resource Management Adventure 3: Leadership & Trade Unions
welcome_lead: Today you'll walk the Tannenbaum–Schmidt continuum and meet trade unions.
meta_desc: IBDP Business Management HRM: Tannenbaum-Schmidt continuum, leadership styles, trade unions, collective bargaining.
final_note: You placed leadership styles on the Tannenbaum-Schmidt continuum and identified the role of trade unions.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Style varies by who decides.

Autocratic — leader dictates: fast in a crisis, demotivating long-term.

Paternalistic — leader decides but explains, like a parent.

Democratic — leader consults and votes: stronger buy-in, slower.

Laissez-faire — leader sets goals then steps back: works for skilled, creative staff.

Tannenbaum and Schmidt (1958) drew a 7-step continuum from manager power to team freedom.

1. Tells → 2. Sells → 3. Suggests → 4. Consults → 5. Joins → 6. Delegates → 7. Abdicates.

Style choice depends on the leader, the team's skill, and the urgency of the task.

Trade unions represent workers, bargaining over pay, hours and conditions.

Collective bargaining replaces individual negotiation, giving workers scale economies.

Industrial action escalates from work-to-rule → overtime ban → go-slow → strike. ACAS or arbitration may mediate.
